name: Battle_ActionModel_ApplyPartParams
summary: Copies the ~30 part parameters (scale, blend, offsets, colours) from the character/model parameter record resolved by 0x0063E5C8 into the action model's f_30..f_DC fields; when randomizeScale is set (descriptor+0x1D) the first scale is multiplied by RNG[0x50,100]/100. Called once from Battle_ActionModel_InitFromDescriptor, so it is a setup copy, not a per-frame update.
evidence: The only caller is Battle_ActionModel_InitFromDescriptor (0.5), which calls it right after func_0027A4E0(self,descriptor) and before Menu_SetOwnerActor; the body is a straight field-by-field copy from func_0063E5C8(dm, self->f_76C & 0xFFFF), with the RNG only scaling one value. That makes 'UpdatePartScale' too narrow and 'Update' wrong.

name: maybe_Model_ApplyFaceAndFrameRows
signature: void maybe_Model_ApplyFaceAndFrameRows(void* self, int face, int frame)
summary: Stores one face-table row (maybe_Data_GetEntry8(face)) and one frame-table row (Svc_GetTableRow(frame)) into the 0x158-byte face record selected by self+2 of the model's face owner; 0xFF means 'leave unchanged'. Model_SetFaceMode calls it with face=0xFF, i.e. only the frame row is refreshed.
evidence: Model_SetFaceMode (0.55) passes 0xFF for face and self->f_1D for frame, and the body writes the two table rows into the f_EC (face) and f_104 (frame) halves of the face record, so 'UpdateFaceAnimation' implied animation playback the function does not perform. The body is still damaged (unaff_r4 holds the face owner), so the name keeps maybe_.

name: Field_RegisterActorModels
summary: Walks the two actor-name tables of the field object (f_27BC/f_27C0 and f_19CC/f_19D0), resolves each relative model name with func_0033D99C(world+0x58, name) and registers the model through Ui_RegisterActor into the field object-manager class lists (+0x1C and +0x20). Field_ResetTalkState calls it while resetting the field talk state.
evidence: Only caller Field_ResetTalkState (0.5) passes the field object at work+8->+0x88; the two loops resolve names through func_0033D99C and call the named Ui_RegisterActor with the Field_ObjectManager lists at +0x1C/+0x20 (FACTS.md), so the models are field actors, not status-window UI.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_SelectRowOrRandom
summary: Stores a 0..9 selection index in the window (+0x11C) and fades the pane at +0x13C; 0..8 are used directly while 9 means 'pick a random one' from the clock-derived value clamped to 9. Ui_LoadingScreen_Create calls it with the save byte at +0x1811, so it chooses which loading-screen variant/hint row to show.
evidence: Ui_LoadingScreen_Create (0.5) passes the save-work byte at +0x1811 (0xFF becomes 0); the body's switch and RNG branch only produce a 0..9 index that is stored at +0x11C and used to toggle the fade at +0x13C. The index's meaning (row vs background variant) is still inferred, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_ListEntry_SyncSprite
summary: Refreshes the sprite of one list entry: in the normal game path it redraws the sprite part f_11 by name, in the alternate path it hides it (mode 5), then advances the list state machine at work+8->+0x90 for that same entry id.
evidence: No direct callers and the callees are still maybe_ (Ui_SpritePart_SetParams, Ui_List_AdvanceState); the body both hides/redraws the sprite part and advances the state machine, so 'RemoveEntryById' named only half of it. Kept maybe_ and renamed to the visible sprite/state sync.

name: maybe_Ui_SubTable_ReleaseEntries
summary: Destroys a three-element array of 0x10-byte sub-entries with element destructor 0x00295660, frees the block and clears the table (pointer +0, state bytes +4/+5 = 0/0xFF). The same array is built by maybe_Gfx_InitTripletTable (0x001E4A40).
evidence: Callers Gfx_ScreenViewEntry_Reset/ResetShort (0.5) plus maybe_Ui_PooledRecord_ResetB and the matching builder maybe_Gfx_InitTripletTable (0x001E4A40) show the three 0x10-byte entries, so 'Rows' is wrong, but the owner (screen-view entry vs pooled record) is still not decided.

name: Event_RebuildIdSet
summary: Rebuilds the byte set of quest/event ids from the save-work state: for every id 0..0x59 it queries the bag/event sub-object at work+0x24A98 and appends the id when its mode is in 2..6. The incremental counterpart Event_UpdateIdSet (0x001E7660) keeps the same set up to date.
evidence: Sibling Event_UpdateIdSet (0.5) maintains exactly the same structure (byte vector at +4/+8, same 2..6 mode window, same bag sub-object at work+0x24A98) and forwards changes to Event_OnQuestFlagChange; Ui_Window_OpenScene calls this at scene start to rebuild it. So 'ItemList_BuildOwnedIndex' was wrong: it is not an item list.

name: Ui_ShopItemList_ResetListPanes
summary: Resets the shop item list before it is opened: re-initialises the list cursor at +0x1E7C, clears the two text layers, re-links the intrusive lists at +0x22AC/+0x230C and the row pane at +0x244C, then applies the item-list mode. Called only from Ui_ShopItemList_OpenList.
evidence: Only caller Ui_ShopItemList_OpenList (0.5) calls it first, before reading the cursor; the body is the same intrusive-list reset as maybe_Ui_ShopWindow_ReleaseListsA (0x001EAC9C) but on the +0x22AC/+0x230C heads, so the 'C' suffix was a placeholder. 'ResetListPanes' describes the visible operations, not a release.

name: maybe_Item_GetStockLevel
signature: void maybe_Item_GetStockLevel(void* result, u32 itemId, int need, void* context)
summary: Compares the required amount of a forge material with three fields of its data-manager record (f_F, f_B and the byte at +7) and writes a 0..3 availability class plus the effective amount into the caller's result record (3 = enough from the first field, 2 = from the second, 1 = only from the byte field, 0 = not enough). Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList uses the classes to build the variant list.
evidence: Caller Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList (0.5) reads result bytes 0..3 and keeps those equal to 1; the record comes from func_0063F108(dm,itemId). The tail is a halt_baddata region, so the output stores after the comparison are only partly reconstructed and the field meanings (bag/owned/required) remain unknown.

name: maybe_Save_SetMaxByte
signature: void maybe_Save_SetMaxByte(int index, u32 value, int update)
summary: Copies the 11-byte save-work block at (work+0x24A98)+0x88ED to the stack, raises the byte at index to value when it is larger (0xFF always writes) and writes the block back. The block is the per-save-slot state block read by SaveSlot_GetStateByte (work+0x2D385+slot) and SaveSlot_GetDisplayByte (+0x2D38A+slot).
evidence: The assembly at 0x001F3084 adds 0x24800+0x298+0x8800+0xED = work+0x2D385, i.e. save work+0x88ED, and SaveSlot_GetStateByte/SaveSlot_GetDisplayByte read the same 11 bytes per slot; the callers (Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList) pass an index that might be a recipe/variant index rather than a save slot, so the index meaning stays unknown.

name: maybe_Save_ClampMinByte
summary: Lowers the byte at (save work+0x88ED)+5+index to value when value is smaller and returns whether it changed; same 11-byte block as maybe_Save_SetMaxByte, written back only when a byte actually changed.
evidence: Same block family as maybe_Save_SetMaxByte (assembly base work+0x2D385); the caller Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList passes the recipe's index and variant value, and the display half of the block is what SaveSlot_GetDisplayByte prints, so the value meaning is still unknown.

name: maybe_FieldParty_ApplySlotAndLayoutBalloons
signature: void maybe_FieldParty_ApplySlotAndLayoutBalloons(PartyGroup* group, int mode, int target, int slot)
summary: Applies a formation slot through the group's virtual +0x40, resets the +0x54 state when mode is 0, and when the group has more than one live member (16-slot array at +0x1C) re-runs Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons for the group. Used both by battle formation setup and the field talk update.
evidence: Callers Battle_ActorAction_SetupFormationScale (0.5) and FieldParty_Talk_Update (0.55); the body's only action beyond the two vtable calls is counting non-null entries of the 16-slot array and calling Battle_Ui_LayoutBalloons. 'SelectFormationSlot' is only the first vtable call, so the name now covers the balloon re-layout.

name: maybe_Actor_QueueEquipmentMessage
signature: void maybe_Actor_QueueEquipmentMessage(void* owner, int slot, void* actor)
summary: Asks the actor's equipment interface for the piece in a slot, maps it to a message id through Ui_LookupMapValueById and enqueues a battle-style message entry for the actor. The only caller, maybe_FieldParty_ApplyAttachmentSet, passes the three attachment slots 0x20/0x21/0x22, so it is the field party's equipment-message queueing path, not a battle-only one.
evidence: The caller passes (group, 0x20/0x21/0x22, actor) and is the field-party attachment updater; the body reads the actor equipment vtable (+0xF8/+0xE8/+0x104/+0xE4) and pushes the resolved id into Battle_MessageQueue_PushEntry. So 'Battle_QueueUnitEquipmentMessage' mislabels the caller side; what the message reports (equip/break) is still inferred.

name: maybe_Model_SyncAttachmentPose
summary: Per-frame attachment/pose sync for a party/actor group: if the candidate model's type is 0x76 or 0x11B and it is present in the group's slot array (+0x1C..), it runs func_001FC370; if the model is type 0x79 it runs Model_SetDirectionToTarget. Called from every field/battle update loop.
evidence: 12 callers, all named update loops (FieldParty_UpdateStateMachine, Battle_ActionSequence_UpdateTurn, Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_Update, Battle_Sequence_Update); the body only tests the model type tags 0x76/0x11B/0x79, looks the model up in the owner's slot array and calls one of two pose helpers, so 'UpdateAttachmentPose' describes the visible work. The called pose helpers are still unnamed.

name: maybe_Menu_ApplySelectedCharacter
summary: Applies a character selection: switches the field status window (work+8->+0x88) to character id and re-attaches the menu actor models of self. Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene0 calls it with the scene record's character byte.
evidence: Only caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene0 (0.5) passes self->f_5C and the scene record's character byte; the body is exactly Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter(work+8->+0x88,id) plus maybe_Menu_RemoveActorAttachments(self). The second half is still a maybe_, so the exact owner ('Menu_') stays unproven.

name: Ui_SceneFlow_SelectStatusCharacter
summary: Forwards a character id to the field status window: Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter(work+8->+0x88, id). It is the small selection wrapper used by the scene-open path, not a jockey-panel visibility setter.
evidence: Only caller Ui_SceneFlow_OpenScene3 (0.5) and the whole body is one Ui_StatusWindow_SelectCharacter call on the object at work+8->+0x88; there is no jockey panel, preview object or visibility flag anywhere, so 'SetPreviewVisible' was wrong.

name: maybe_Battle_PickRandomPartyActor
summary: Collects up to 16 valid battle actors into a local array and returns one at random (or 0 when none qualify). When context+0x10 is 0 it scans the four unit lists at battle work +0x4298+i*0x1C requiring virtual +0x18; otherwise it scans only the party list at +0x4260 requiring both +0x18 and +0x24, then rolls the battle RNG for the final index.
evidence: The three callers are Battle_Message_BuildActorRowBig, Battle_Ui_RunMessageRowCommand and Battle_ActorAction_UpdateReaction, all of which need a random actor for a message/reaction; the body rolls func_001CA474 and walks the four unit lists from FACTS.md. Whether 'party' is the right scope is still unproven (the lists may include guests/enemies).

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_SetUnitEntryValue
signature: void maybe_Battle_Ui_SetUnitEntryValue(void* self, u32 index, u32 value)
summary: Looks up the battle unit at index in the battle party/unit list at self+0x4254 and forwards a packed value to its UI controller virtual +0xB0. The six callers are all battle/field slot refreshers (Battle_Equip_UpdateWeaponSlot/ArmourSlot, Battle_Ui_InitSlots, FieldParty_Ui_RefreshMemberSlot), so the value most likely identifies the entry/slot shown on that unit.
evidence: self+0x4254 is the first battle unit list (FACTS.md), func_002AB37C resolves the object handle, and the callers are the weapon/armour slot refresh paths; the body passes the value as one 3-byte packed argument to vfunc +0xB0 and never interprets it, so which value it is stays inferred.

name: Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_CalcAnchor
summary: Computes the anchor of a member widget: for each active slot it projects the slot's position through virtual +0xB8, tracks the minimum/maximum X and Z, and writes their midpoints (plus the fixed Y from self+0xA0) into out.
evidence: Only caller is the named Battle_Ui_MemberWidget_UpdateEffects (0.5); the body's arithmetic is exactly a min/max bounding box over the projected slot positions followed by writes of the midpoints to out->f_2C/f_30/f_34, and Svc_ResolveObjectHandle/Container_FindObjectByTypeIdJ are the per-slot lookups. 'CalcAnchor' is an honest description of that midpoint.

name: maybe_Menu_InitEffectParamsBase
summary: Base effect-parameter initialiser for a menu page: clears f_424A and, only when sub-menu flag f_4E6F is set, registers the 0x13/0x15/0x14 effect ids, runs Menu_InitCursorEffectParams and starts the category BGM. The cursor draw-step ids 9/10 are added only by the companion 0x0020F330.
evidence: The body differs from 0x0020F330 only by not creating the two cursor draw-step ids 9/10 and by not setting f_4211; the shared core (0x13/0x15/0x14 + Menu_InitCursorEffectParams + category BGM) is identical, so it is the base variant of the same page initialiser. No caller identifies the page.

name: maybe_Menu_InitEffectParamsWithCursor
summary: Page effect-parameter initialiser that registers the 0x13/0x15/0x14 effect ids, the two cursor draw-step ids 9/10, finishes the parameter set with func_003D1144, sets f_4211=0xFF and starts the category BGM. The 9/10 pair distinguishes it from the base variant 0x0020E628.
evidence: No callers; the body is the base initialiser 0x0020E628 plus Gfx_EffectParams_Create(9)/(10), f_4211=0xFF and func_003D1144. The page it belongs to is still unidentified.

name: Menu_TeardownWindow
summary: Tears the menu window down: releases either the 2D sub-object at +0x47A0 or the 3D layout at +0x4330 depending on f_4244, destroys the owner object at +0x10, releases the five 0x40-byte icon-model load tasks, updates the selection window and resets the pending-selection counter.
evidence: Caller Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0.5) and callees Ui_Window_ReleaseSubObject, Menu_WindowLayout_Teardown, Menu_IconModelLoadTask_Update and Menu_UpdateSelectionWindow cover every step; the five-iteration task release and the f_432C counter reset are visible, so 'TeardownWindow' matches the whole body.

name: Ui_IconWidget_RecreateSubObject
summary: Recreates the sub-object host of an icon widget: destroys the current object at +0x114 through its vtable, allocates 0x30 bytes from the widget's allocator and constructs a new Ui_SubObjectHost with the requested id. Called from Ui_IconWidget_Redraw when the icon must be rebuilt.
evidence: Callers Ui_IconWidget_Redraw (0.5) and Field2D_JumpTableEntry4; the body is release-vtable-then-Mem_AllocAligned_2(0x30)+Ui_SubObjectHost_Ctor(id), i.e. it recreates the sub-object host, not an arbitrary 'icon' (the icon meaning comes from the caller).

name: maybe_Menu_TalkParty_WaitPanels
summary: Waits until the 24 embedded sub-panels at self+0x1C report done; then, once a button is pressed or the wait timed out, closes the field UI core (func_002D2440 plus the +0x1C object's virtuals) and creates the map cursor when self+0x9C is set.
evidence: No callers; the 24-slot wait loop and the UI-core close are visible, and maybe_Ui_CreateMapCursor is named, but the TalkParty ownership still comes only from the neighbouring panel creator 0x002175BC.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ReleaseChildAndRequestMode
summary: Window dismissal hook: frees the embedded child object at f_C4, and when the layout at f_94 has its auto-close byte +0x8D set and requested is 0, raises the global screen-switch request flag at 0x007A9A90 and highlights the window's page.
evidence: Callers Party_Status_SetEnabled (0.5) and Ui_SetModeAndNotify (0.5) use it as the deferred close request; the consumer of the global 0x007A9A90 flag is still unknown, so the named effect (release child + request mode) stays a description.

name: maybe_Font_QueryAtlasCellAtGridPos
signature: u32 maybe_Font_QueryAtlasCellAtGridPos(void* self, const char* text, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Looks up the font-atlas cell at the sprite's 8-scaled grid position (f_78*8, f_7C*8) and queries its glyph class in the device font context at +0xF50. Returns 1; no draw call appears, so it is a query/lookup, not a glyph plot.
evidence: Both callees are Font_Atlas_LookupCell and Font_GetGlyphClass on Gfx_GetContext()+0xF50, and the function has no callers and no draw/vtable call, so 'PlotGlyphCell' described an action the body does not perform. The purpose of the lookup is unknown.

name: maybe_Ui_Part_InitChildWindow
summary: Initialises a part's child row/window at +0x124: formats it through Ui_ItemRow_Format, hides the null-button state, sets the animation reference at +0x174 to its frame, and finally calls the owner virtual +0x24. The object is the same 0x1C8-byte part built by Ui_Part_Ctor (0x00240980), not a standalone list.
evidence: The only caller is Ui_SpritePart_CreateFromDesc (0.5), which allocates the 0x1C8-byte block and calls Ui_Part_Ctor on it; this function then formats the child at +0x124 and uses the anim ref at +0x174, so 'Ui_List_UpdateSubWidgets' described the wrong owner. The exact child class (Ui_QuestWindow_Ctor is installed there) is still unclear.

name: Ui_Part_Ctor
summary: Constructor of the 0x1C8-byte UI part object: installs vtable 0x0075C82C, marks the two handle fields empty and constructs the embedded child window at +0x124 (Ui_QuestWindow_Ctor) and the animation-reference list at +0x50 (Ui_AnimRefList_Ctor).
evidence: Only caller Ui_SpritePart_CreateFromDesc (0.5) allocates the block and immediately calls this on the fresh memory; the vtable install and two sub-constructors are the standard constructor shape, and both sub-constructors are named now.

name: Game_GetDisplayModeFlag
summary: Returns the first byte of the game work's 2D/3D display-mode pair at work+0x27508; callers read it with the second byte at +0x27509 to choose between a sprite and a model (monster book and item candidate lists).
evidence: The body only reads Game_GetWork()+0x27508, so the Ui_ prefix was wrong; 15 callers include Ui_MonsterBook_BuildEntryList/SelectModel (0.5) and eight Item_BuildCandidateList variants that pick sprite vs model. Whether the non-zero value means 2D or 3D is not proven, so the name says 'display mode flag' rather than naming a direction.

name: maybe_Ui_MonsterBookEntry_Ctor
summary: Constructor fragment that installs vtable 0x0075C904 on the object, validates the weak handle at +0x11D4 against the type table and allocates/constructs the embedded 0x98-byte object at the caller's slot. Ghidra loses control flow after 0x002447B8, so the tail is missing.
evidence: The body is damaged (unaff_r9/unaff_r10 and halt_baddata) and no named caller or neighbour references it; only the vtable 0x0075C904 and the +0x11D4 field tie it to the 0x11xx monster-book object family. Kept maybe_ at 0.3.

name: Event_AddCommonHandler
summary: Appends a handler record to the event handler vector at self+0x98, stores the literal name "common" in it and copies the event descriptor handle pair from self+0x30. Event_ApplyScenarioJumpSettings registers it while applying jump settings.
evidence: The body stores the string literal s_common_0025664c into the new element and binds self+0x30; the only caller is Event_ApplyScenarioJumpSettings (0.5). That is exactly 'add the common handler', so the old 'select current handler slot' reading was wrong.

name: maybe_Event_OpenRuraPatternPane
summary: Handles the result of the Rura (travel) pattern selection: when Script_CallSelectRuraPattern returns anything other than 1 it builds the 0x2A page record, binds it into self+0xCC0 and pushes it into the jumon (spell) window at self+0x13C; when it returns 1 it starts the 0x27->0x31 widget transition instead.
evidence: No callers; the named callee Script_CallSelectRuraPattern supplies the 'Rura pattern' term and Ui_JumonWindow_PushPane the pane push, and func_002BBAD0(0x2A) supplies the page record. Whether the non-1 branch opens or closes the pane is still inferred, so maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageArgWidget_InitSlot2
summary: Initialises an existing message-argument child widget: resets the helper at +0x820, drains the old children, selects self+0x918, disables the core view object, binds message argument slot 2 through func_001F0BE4(2) and shows the sub-widget at +0x4754.
evidence: The body operates on an existing widget (releases children, selects +0x918, binds func_001F0BE4(2), fades in +0x4754) and never allocates or installs a vtable, so 'Ctor' was wrong; the argument-slot binding is the only thing that identifies it as the message-argument widget.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_ChooseStateByItemFlags
summary: Chooses the recipe-book window state from two progress flags of the selected recipe: state 0x10 (and f_11D9=1) when the slot-state flag is clear, state 0x12 when the second flag is 0 and state 0x11 otherwise; then applies the chosen state through the state object at +0x11C.
evidence: No callers; the flag getters are the named SaveSlot_IsUsed and maybe_Save_GetBlockByteEquals3 on self->f_11E4->f_A8, and the three state ids 0x10/0x11/0x12 sit next to the 0x09..0x0F states that Ui_RecipeBook_BuildVariantList pushes. What the two flags mean (recipe known vs item owned) is not decoded.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_RefreshFromFlags
summary: Refreshes a recipe-book window from the save-progress flags: re-reads the three progress masks, snapshots the previous values (f_10B8=f_10B4, f_10D8=f_10D4, f_10F4=f_10F0), clears the selected bits and rebuilds the visible state/byte vector accordingly.
evidence: Only caller is Ui_TrainingMessage_ReleaseTables (0.5), not a recipe-book function, but the body reads maybe_Save_TestProgressMask(1/2/4), Flag_GetGlobal1 and maybe_Save_GetFlag275a4 and rewrites the f_10B4..f_1118 recipe-window fields. The 'recipe book' owner is therefore inferred from the field layout and Ui_RecipeBook_RefreshVisibility.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_AdvanceScriptCmd06B
summary: Damaged 20-byte Thumb variant of the 'advance script' update record: after the idle gate it dispatches command 6 on the state object at +0x11C and, when that reports progress, calls its +0x10 slot. The object pointer arrives as unaff_r4, so only the call sequence matches 0x00264048.
evidence: The body is truncated to 0x14 bytes and reads unaff_r4 plus extra arg registers, so nothing beyond the identical call sequence to 0x00264048 can be verified; kept maybe_ at 0.3 as the damaged-decompilation case from FACTS.md.

name: maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_SelectRecipe
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_RecipeBook_SelectRecipe(int recipeIndex, int window, u32 arg3, int row)
summary: Selects a recipe row: when Recipe_CanCraft(recipeIndex*0x11) reports it cannot be crafted it dismisses the row object and returns 1; otherwise it fills the detail record at window+0x1E4, builds the material list and party entries and dispatches command 5 to the state object at +0x11C.
evidence: Recipe_CanCraft and Ui_RecipeBook_BuildMaterialList/FillPartyEntries pin this to the recipe-row selection path, but the decompilation reads unaff_r5/r6/r7/r8 and in_r12, so the argument roles and the tail callback setup are damaged. Kept maybe_ at 0.35.

name: Ui_TargetWindow_SetSlotCharacter
signature: void Ui_TargetWindow_SetSlotCharacter(TargetWindow* self, int clearFirst, u32 characterId, u32 slotIndex)
summary: Sets the character shown in target slot slotIndex (0..3) of the four 0x470-byte slots through Ui_StatusWindow_SetCharacter(self + slotIndex*0x470 + 0x154, characterId, 0, work+0x432C). When clearFirst is 0 it also resets slot 0 to 0xFF with a fade-out before fading the widget back in.
evidence: Three callers, including the named Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshMemberIds (0.5); the body's four-slot stride 0x470, the 0xFF clear and the calls to Ui_StatusWindow_SetCharacter are all visible, and the only unnamed callee is the fade helper 0x0029126C.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleTargetWindow_ScrollPage
summary: Page-cursor handler for the battle target window: counts the party list plus the four enemy page lists, wraps the cursor to the last page when page+delta would go below zero, refreshes the pager through func_0043F200 and re-enables the text items.
evidence: No callers; the count/wrap logic is clear and uses the battle unit lists from FACTS.md, but delta is only used for the wrap test and the pager helper func_0043F200 is unnamed, so 'ScrollPage' remains a description of the visible cursor update.

name: maybe_Ui_BattleTargetWindow_SetPage
signature: void maybe_Ui_BattleTargetWindow_SetPage(u32 self, u32 current, u32 total, u32 arg4)
summary: Small pager helper: forwards the current page, the total and self to the shared pager func_0043F200 and commits the result through Ui_TextLayer_UpdateEnabledItems.
evidence: No callers; the 34-byte Thumb body has the same func_0043F200 + Ui_TextLayer_UpdateEnabledItems tail as 0x002696B4, so it is that window's pager setter, but the 'BattleTargetWindow' owner is still inferred from the sibling only.

name: BattleUnit_GetLinkedModelByIndex
summary: Resolves a model from a battle unit's linked model-slot lists: it first honours the special entry at +0x73C, otherwise walks the +0x704/+0x708 or +0x71C/+0x724 list to the requested live slot index and returns the entry's +0xC model pointer.
evidence: The named callers Ui_ArcListWindow_UpdateScrollAim and Ui_ArcListWindow_LayoutEntriesByHeight pass a unit object and immediately read the returned model's f_110/f_768 fields; the body only walks the same +0x704/+0x708 slot-entry lists used by Actor_UnlinkFromParentList3 and checks the entry's vtable +0x14 liveness, with no AI/tactics state, so the BattleAi_ prefix was wrong.

name: maybe_Actor_UnlinkFromParentList
summary: Unlinks the model from the first family of owner slot lists (self+0x730 and the owner's +0x724 list), frees the entry, recounts the surviving active entries and stores a random surviving index in the owner's +0x738 cursor.
evidence: Named callers Model_AdvanceAnimFrames (0.55), Actor_ResetModelSlots (0.5) and maybe_Model_SetSlotState call it together with the three sibling unlink helpers (0x279B70/0x279D3C/0x279E64) when a model is removed or an animation ends; each sibling handles a different slot-list family, so the family name is right but which of the four lists this one owns is not identified.

name: maybe_Actor_UnlinkFromParentList3
summary: Mirror of 0x002793C4 for the second slot-list family (self+0x714 and the owner's +0x704 list): unlinks the model entry, frees it, recounts active entries and stores a random surviving index in the owner's +0x71C cursor.
evidence: Same call sites as 0x002793C4 (Model_AdvanceAnimFrames, Actor_ResetModelSlots, maybe_Model_SetSlotState) plus Battle_ActionSequence_WaitUnitState; the body is the +0x714/+0x704 mirror of the first helper, so the family is confirmed but the list role (3D vs 2D or by unit kind) is still unknown.

name: maybe_Actor2D_BuildPartSpriteList
signature: void maybe_Actor2D_BuildPartSpriteList(void* self, u32 count, const void* partArray)
summary: Damaged Thumb fragment that repeats the part-sprite loop of 0x0028EFEC: for each part entry it creates an Actor2D sprite with defaults, stores it in the f_2D0 array, attaches it and finally clears f_2D4/f_2D8/f_2DC.
evidence: Every parameter arrives as unaff_rX (damaged decompilation), so only the callee set (Actor2D_CreateSpriteWithDefaults, Gfx_CreateSpriteMesh, Gfx_SpriteActor_CreateFromTable) and the identical epilogue tie it to 0x0028EFEC; the exact build step cannot be verified.

name: Ui_PokerCards_ConfirmSelection
summary: Confirm handler of the poker minigame row: selects the row in the list, maps the row state 0..9 to one of the cue ids 0x3A/0x3B/0x3C through maybe_Ui_Cue_Start, plays the panel animation from the table and copies the shared style template; state -1 routes to the panel-state advance.
evidence: It shares the poker table at 0x0072A8EC/0x0072A904 with the confident Ui_PokerCards_ToggleCardHold (0.8) and Ui_PokerCards_ResetCardHoldFlags (0.75); the switch on the same f_E5 row state, the five card-slot loop and Ui_List_SelectRow/Ui_Panel_PlayAnimFromTable confirm the poker-card reading. No direct callers because it is a table entry.

name: maybe_Ui_PokerCards_UpdateSlotHighlight
summary: Cursor handler for the five poker card slots: when row[2] is a multiple of 5 it refreshes the current slot, when row[2]-5 is a multiple of 5 (and below 0x1A) it sends message 0xE9C, and past 0x27 it recounts the five visible flags, re-selects the row and updates the mode.
evidence: The callee set (Ui_List_SelectRow, Ui_PokerTable_SetupCards, Ui_PokerWindow_SetAllCardVisibility, Ui_PokerCards_ApplyRowTransform) pins it to the poker table, but the 'highlight' wording is inferred from the index/count logic and the two small helpers func_0023F880/func_001E3C70 are unnamed.

name: Ui_PokerCards_ResetSlots
summary: Resets a poker row to its empty state: sets all five slot flags, clears the model slots through the five slot helpers, resets the list selection to 0xFF, re-applies mode 0 and plays the open animation, then restores the shared row template.
evidence: The five-iteration reset loop and the callees Ui_PokerTable_UpdateCardSlots, Ui_PokerWindow_SetAllCardVisibility, maybe_Ui_PokerCards_SetMode0/PlayOpenAnim pin it to the poker-card row, and the two live variants are confident poker functions; only the caller maybe_Ui_PanelRow_ResetAnimationStateB is weak.

name: maybe_Ui_GridCursor_HandleInput
summary: Input handler for the grid cursor at self+0x420: the cancel bit pops the dive-form pane, the confirm bits ask the controller for the chosen cell (0xFF = none) and commit it, and the direction bits compute the next cell through Ui_GridCursor_CalcNextIndex and bind it through Ui_List_SelectEntryById.
evidence: The object layout is the dive form's (+0x134 pane stack, +0x37D4 state) and the named callees Ui_DiveForm_PopPane/Ui_GridCursor_CalcNextIndex/Ui_List_SelectEntryById fix the generic cursor role, but the neighbouring helpers still carry maybe_ names so the owner class is not confirmed.

name: maybe_Event_SelectPartyStatusPageEx
summary: Event handler that reads the page pair from the event object (virtual +0xCC and self[0x58]+0x126), selects it through Party_Status_SelectPage on the overlay manager at work+8->+0x48 and then calls Party_Status_ResumeFieldActors(...,1).
evidence: No callers; the body is complete and matches the sibling maybe_Event_SelectPartyStatusPage at 0x002B5900 (symbols_recovered.json), which is why the Ex suffix is kept. The page byte at self[0x58]+0x126 is read but its meaning is not decoded.

name: maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyIconStyles
signature: void maybe_Ui_MessageWindow_ApplyIconStyles(UiMessageWindow* self, u32 messageId, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Item-icon styling for a message window: caches the id at +0x4C and returns when unchanged; resolves it through Item_LookupRecord, applies the default window skin when the id is not an item, otherwise dispatches the message commands and picks the icon/effect style from the item's equipment ranges (0xA4..0x9BF, 0xB19..0xB1C) and category byte.
evidence: Item_LookupRecord on the id proves this is item code, not text, and the body uses the equipment ranges from FACTS.md; the only caller Ui_Widget_ResolveChildPointerByName does not say which window, and the style helpers maybe_Ui_MessageCmd_Apply/maybe_Ui_Pane_CreateEffectForItemId are still maybe_, so the 'IconStyles' reading stays a description.
